purpose: Original kingdom-inspired chess sprite atlases; fictional characters, not exact historical reconstructions.

prompts.japanese:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production chess-game transparent sprite atlas, not a poster.
Make exactly 12 isolated full-body miniature chess character sprites, on a genuinely transparent alpha background, in a rigorously spaced 6-column by 2-row grid on a landscape 1536x1024 canvas. Each cell is 256x512 pixels, with at least 25 pixels of empty margin around every character. No text, labels, grid lines, scenic background, floor, drop shadows, plinths, floating decorations or detached props.
Column order in BOTH rows is KING, QUEEN, BISHOP-as-court-advisor, mounted KNIGHT on a horse, ROOK-as-compact-fortress, PAWN-as-simple-foot-soldier. Top row WHITE army in ivory/light silver garments with muted colour accents; bottom row BLACK army in deep charcoal/dark steel garments with muted colour accents. Do not associate skin tone with chess side: use the same natural ethnic variety on both sides. White and Black clothes must be strongly distinguishable on a board.
Royal King and Queen: most upright and tallest, dignified fictional adults in recognizably different royal costume and headgear; Queen is nearly as tall as King. Bishop/advisor, mounted knight and fortress: visibly shorter than royalty. Pawn: shortest AND narrowest, very simple infantry outfit, no crown, no cape, no horse, no elaborate shoulder plates, only a small practical weapon/shield kept below head level. Pawn is an adult soldier rendered smaller, not a child. All feet/bottoms align on a common baseline within each row. Full figures and all horse legs intact, natural horse anatomy, no cropping or overlap between cells.
Style: polished hand-painted 3D-like strategy-game miniatures, cohesive illustrative realism, warm soft studio light, restrained detail readable on a phone chessboard, distinct silhouettes and clean edges. Characters near-front three-quarter view, looking slightly to the viewer's left. The same illustrative style and scale logic for both armies. Original respectful designs inspired by historical clothing, not portraits of real named people or modern stereotypes.
Theme: Japanese Shogunate, late-medieval/Momoyama-inspired court and armour. Ivory/gold versus charcoal/deep indigo. King: imposing samurai lord in layered lacquered lamellar armour, silk outer coat, restrained gold-crested kabuto helmet, sheathed sword. Queen: dignified noblewoman in rich layered silk court robes, formal updo and a tasteful gold hair ornament, holding a folded fan. Bishop/advisor: court retainer in broad-shouldered formal robe and compact eboshi cap, scroll at waist. Knight: samurai rider in light lamellar armour on a compact sturdy horse. Rook: simple Japanese castle keep, white plaster and dark tiled stepped roofs. Pawn: plain ashigaru foot soldier, simple low conical jingasa hat, modest cuirass and straight trousers, short spear held with its point below head height. No giant antlers, no flags or floating cherry blossoms.

Theme: Mongolian Khans, 13th-century Mongol/Yuan court and cavalry inspiration. Ivory/pale gold with turquoise accents versus charcoal/bronze with deep blue accents. King: dignified khan in long brocade robe fastened at one side with a wide belted cummerbund, high leather boots and modest rounded royal cap, compact ceremonial sword. Queen: elegant khatun in ample long brocade robe with tall structured gugu headdress, restrained jewellery, still completely inside her cell. Bishop/advisor: scholarly court envoy in plain belted robe and modest cap, small scroll held low. Knight: skilled mounted archer in lamellar armour on a compact steppe horse, bow lowered below head height. Rook: compact square walled gatehouse from a steppe imperial capital with a modest tiled roof, not a giant tent. Pawn: simple adult foot guard in plain belted knee-length robe, boots and modest cap, small bow held low. Respectful natural Mongolian features, no exaggerated grimaces, no universal fur outfit, no barbarian caricature.

Theme: Egyptian Pharaohs, ancient New Kingdom-inspired royal court and soldiers. Ivory linen/pale sandstone/gold with lapis accents versus charcoal linen/dark basalt/bronze with lapis accents. King: tall dignified pharaoh with blue-and-gold striped nemes-style royal headdress, broad gold collar and long pleated ceremonial linen garment, small crook held across chest. Queen: tall regal woman with an elegant flat-topped blue-and-gold royal crown, broad collar and long fitted pleated linen robe. Bishop/advisor: royal scribe in plain linen robe with low headcloth and closed papyrus roll at waist, no animal head. Knight: original chess adaptation of an Egyptian royal guard on a compact horse with simple linen saddlecloth; keep it visually shorter than royalty. Rook: compact sandstone Egyptian pylon gateway with symmetrical sloping walls and subtle geometric carving. Pawn: very simple adult infantryman in short linen kilt, low headband, small oval shield and short spear both below head height. Natural varied Egyptian skin tones on BOTH armies, no mummies, gods, monster heads or caricatures. This is a chess-themed historical inspiration, not an archaeological reconstruction.

Theme: Arab Caliphate, Abbasid-inspired court and military clothing, dignified fictional adult characters. Ivory and pale gold garments with emerald accents versus charcoal and bronze garments with deep emerald accents; two stylized chess colourways, not a claim of official historical uniform. King: tall court ruler in a layered buttoned caftan and flowing ceremonial outer robe, full wrapped turban over a soft cap, restrained gold trim and short sheathed sword. Queen: tall court noblewoman in a dignified long layered silk gown, fine jewellery and an elegant light headcloth secured with a subtle jewelled band; no exposed midriff or dancer costume. Bishop/advisor: learned court scholar in simple layered robe and modest turban, closed manuscript held at waist. Knight: mounted cavalryman in mail and a modest conical helmet, on a compact horse, short sword lowered. Rook: compact medieval city fortress gate with square crenellations and a simple arched entrance, no mosque or minaret. Pawn: very simple adult infantryman in plain knee-length tunic, belt, simple low cap, short sword and small round shield kept below head height; no elaborate turban or cape. No pseudo-Arabic writing, religious text, sacred symbols, modern checkered keffiyeh, Ottoman fez or caricatures.

King: tall dignified shah-like fictional ruler in layered floral silk brocade robe, broad decorative sash and full wrapped turban with a modest aigrette, compact sheathed sword. Queen: tall elegant royal woman in a long layered brocade robe over chemise and trousers, light square headcloth secured with a narrow silk ribbon and pearl chin-band, refined gold jewellery, no dancer outfit. Bishop/advisor: court scholar in a simple long robe, sash and low wrapped turban, small book held at waist. Knight: mounted warrior in mail and a conical metal helmet on a compact horse, modest saddlecloth, curved saber held down below head. Rook: compact Persian fortress gate with restrained turquoise tiled ornament and two squat defensive towers, not a mosque. Pawn: very simple adult foot guard in a plain belted robe, trousers and low conical helmet, small round shield and short saber held low. No Ottoman fez, modern flags, oversized feathers, pseudo-writing, sacred text or caricatures. Keep Persian and Arab sets visually distinct through robe layering, headdresses and architectural details.

Ivory and polished silver with crimson/gold accents versus charcoal and dark steel with deep crimson/bronze accents. King: tall dignified crowned monarch with a modest gold open crown, polished plate armour, rich long ceremonial mantle and sheathed longsword. Queen: tall regal woman in a long fitted medieval gown, flowing over-robe and elegant gold open crown over a restrained veil; distinguish her rounded dress silhouette clearly from king armour. Bishop/advisor: learned court chancellor in long academic robes and low cap, closed book at waist, no giant staff. Knight: mounted plate-armoured knight on a compact horse with simple caparison, lowered sword, no raised lance or banners. Rook: compact square English stone castle keep with flat crenellations and a small arched door. Pawn: very simple adult foot archer in a plain padded jack, modest soft cap, short trousers and boots, a compact bow held low beside body, no longbow rising above the head. No modern uniforms or flags, no crowns on foot soldiers.

King: tall crowned monarch in a long blue-accented royal surcoat and ceremonial mantle over fine plate armour, open gold crown with simple lily-shaped points, compact sword held downward. Queen: tall dignified queen in a sweeping long court gown with fitted bodice, gold crown and restrained veil, simple lily-inspired embroidered details. Bishop/advisor: royal counsellor in a dark-blue-accented long robe and soft medieval cap, small sealed scroll held low. Knight: mounted armoured chevalier on a compact horse with blue-accented caparison, short lowered sword, no lance or banner. Rook: compact French castle tower with a conical slate roof and small round turrets, clearly different from an English square crenellated keep. Pawn: very simple adult man-at-arms in a modest padded tunic, small sallet-style helmet and plain leg armour, small shield and short sword below head height. No oversized plumes, no flags, no Napoleonic or modern uniforms. Keep the art and natural anatomy elegant, not caricature.
